senses.gloss: A gap or clear space between two people, things, or positions.
examples: There was no *daylight* between the mayor and the governor on the budget.
The lead runner opened up some *daylight* between herself and the pack.
You could see *daylight* under the door where it didn't sit flush.

senses.gloss: A formal public statement or announcement.
examples: The colonies signed their *declaration* of independence in 1776.
Congress has not issued a formal *declaration* of war since 1942.
His speech was a *declaration* that he intends to run again.

senses.gloss: A medal or award given for bravery or long service.
examples: The old sergeant wore every *decoration* he had earned overseas.
She received the country's highest military *decoration*.
His dress uniform was covered in *decorations* from three campaigns.

senses.gloss: The process of reaching a conclusion by reasoning from the facts you already have.
examples: By simple *deduction*, she figured out who had taken the keys.
The detective's *deduction* turned out to be exactly right.
He reached the answer by *deduction* rather than guesswork.

senses.gloss: A person who publicly argues in support of someone or something.
examples: She is a fierce *defender* of free speech.
Even his *defenders* admit that the plan has problems.
The senator became the leading *defender* of the program in Congress.

senses.gloss: The sharpness and clarity of an image, a sound, or an outline.
examples: The new screen shows every detail in high *definition*.
The old photograph has lost some of its *definition*.
Months of training gave his arms real muscle *definition*.

senses.gloss: The act of giving part of your work or authority to someone else.
examples: Good managers get better at *delegation* over time.
The *delegation* of authority to local offices sped everything up.
He does everything himself because *delegation* makes him nervous.

senses.gloss: Fineness or fragility of structure, texture, or build.
examples: The *delicacy* of the lace made it impossible to machine wash.
She admired the *delicacy* of the hand-painted cups.
For all her *delicacy*, she was surprisingly strong.

senses.gloss: Care and tact in handling something that could easily upset people.
examples: The subject has to be raised with some *delicacy*.
He handled the firing with real *delicacy*.
Negotiations of this kind call for patience and *delicacy*.

senses.gloss: Failure to pay a debt or bill on time.
examples: Mortgage *delinquency* rates rose for the third straight month.
The account went into *delinquency* after two missed payments.
The bank watches *delinquencies* of ninety days or more very closely.

senses.gloss: The birth of a baby.
examples: She had an easy *delivery* and went home the next day.
Labor and *delivery* is on the fourth floor of the hospital.
Both *deliveries* were by cesarean section.

senses.gloss: The way someone speaks lines, tells a joke, or gives a speech.
examples: The jokes were fine, but his *delivery* was flat.
Her *delivery* was slow and clear enough for everyone to follow.
The speech was good on paper; the *delivery* ruined it.

senses.gloss: The statistical make-up of a population, such as its age, income, and racial mix.
examples: The *demographics* of the town have changed a lot in ten years.
The chain studies the *demographics* of a neighborhood before opening a store.
Shifting *demographics* are reshaping the school district.

senses.gloss: A practical showing of how something works or how something is done.
examples: The salesman gave us a quick *demonstration* of the mixer.
There's a free cooking *demonstration* at the store on Saturday.
After a short *demonstration*, the students tried it themselves.

senses.gloss: The face value of a bill, coin, or stamp.
examples: The machine only takes bills in small *denominations*.
Please bring the cash in mixed *denominations*.
The post office sells stamps in several *denominations*.

senses.gloss: A feature or quality that several people or things have in common.
examples: The common *denominator* in all three robberies was a stolen white van.
Cheap shows aimed at the lowest common *denominator* fill the afternoon schedule.
If there's a common *denominator* among the winners, it's hard work.

senses.gloss: An area of activity or responsibility that belongs to a particular person.
examples: Cooking is my husband's *department*, not mine.
Sorry, that's not my *department* — you'll want to ask Rita.
The car is great on gas but lacking in the comfort *department*.

senses.gloss: A change from what is usual or expected.
examples: The new album is a real *departure* for the band.
Serving pie at a wedding is a nice *departure* from tradition.
Her ruling was a sharp *departure* from earlier decisions.

senses.gloss: The laying down of sand, mud, or other material by wind or water.
examples: The delta grew through centuries of silt *deposition*.
Geologists study the *deposition* of sediment along the riverbed.
Layers formed by slow *deposition* are visible in the canyon wall.

senses.gloss: A long period when an economy is very weak and many people are out of work.
examples: My grandmother grew up during the *depression* and never wasted food.
Economists argued over whether the slump was a recession or a *depression*.
The *depression* of the 1930s left a quarter of workers without jobs.

senses.gloss: A hollow or sunken place in a surface.
examples: Rainwater collected in a shallow *depression* in the yard.
There was a *depression* in the mattress where he always slept.
The map shows a wide *depression* between the two ridges.

senses.gloss: An area of low air pressure that brings unsettled weather, especially the early stage of a tropical storm.
examples: The storm weakened into a tropical *depression* before it reached land.
Forecasters are watching a *depression* forming off the coast.
The *depression* is expected to strengthen into a hurricane by Friday.

senses.gloss: A small group of troops or police sent away from the main body for a particular job.
examples: A *detachment* of marines guarded the embassy.
The colonel sent a small *detachment* ahead to scout the bridge.
Two *detachments* were posted at the crossing overnight.

senses.gloss: The coming loose or separating of one thing from another.
examples: Sudden flashes of light can be a sign of retinal *detachment*.
The crash was caused by the *detachment* of a wheel.
Surgeons repaired the *detachment* the same afternoon.

senses.gloss: The holding of someone in custody by the police or immigration authorities.
examples: He spent six months in *detention* before the hearing.
The family was released from immigration *detention* last week.
Her lawyers argued that the *detention* was unlawful.

senses.gloss: The act of officially deciding or establishing a fact or an amount.
examples: The *determination* of the cause of the fire took several weeks.
The agency's *determination* that she qualified arrived in the mail.
A final *determination* of benefits will be made by the state.

senses.gloss: A new event or piece of news that changes a situation.
examples: We'll bring you the latest *developments* as they come in.
There has been an important *development* in the case.
Recent *developments* forced the company to change its plans.

senses.gloss: A group of houses or buildings put up together on one piece of land.
examples: They bought a house in a new *development* outside town.
The *development* off the highway has two hundred units.
Several *developments* went up where the orchards used to be.

senses.gloss: A serious exchange of views between two sides who are trying to reach agreement.
examples: The two sides have agreed to open a *dialogue*.
Years of quiet *dialogue* finally produced a deal.
The mayor called for an honest *dialogue* about policing.

senses.gloss: A soft dome-shaped device a woman puts in place to prevent pregnancy.
examples: Her doctor fitted her for a *diaphragm*.
She keeps the *diaphragm* in a small plastic case.
A *diaphragm* has to be used together with spermicide.

senses.gloss: The ring of blades in a camera lens that controls how much light gets through.
examples: Closing the *diaphragm* keeps more of the scene in focus.
This lens has a nine-blade *diaphragm*.
Open the *diaphragm* wider when the light is poor.

senses.gloss: The amount left when one number is subtracted from another.
examples: The *difference* between twelve and five is seven.
Subtract the smaller number and write the *difference* below the line.
The *difference* between the two bids was almost ten thousand dollars.

senses.gloss: A disagreement or quarrel between people.
examples: The two brothers finally settled their *differences*.
They had a *difference* of opinion about where to eat.
Let's set our *differences* aside and finish the job.

senses.gloss: An aspect or side of a situation.
examples: Her illness added a new *dimension* to the family's problems.
The report ignores the human *dimension* of the layoffs.
There is a political *dimension* to the decision as well.

senses.gloss: In stories and science fiction, a world or plane of existence separate from our own.
examples: The kids fall through a doorway into another *dimension*.
The show is about creatures from a parallel *dimension*.
He claims the machine can move objects between *dimensions*.

senses.gloss: A person or thing that is hopelessly out of date.
examples: My old laptop is a complete *dinosaur*.
He calls himself a *dinosaur* because he still writes checks.
The industry is full of *dinosaurs* who refuse to go online.

senses.gloss: Skill and tact in dealing with people without upsetting them.
examples: It took some *diplomacy* to get the two of them in the same room.
She handled the complaint with real *diplomacy*.
A little *diplomacy* would have prevented the whole argument.

senses.gloss: Instructions telling you how to get somewhere or how to do something.
examples: We stopped at a gas station to ask for *directions*.
Follow the *directions* on the back of the box.
The *directions* said to bake it for forty minutes.

senses.gloss: Guidance or control over what someone does, or a clear sense of purpose.
examples: The choir sang under the *direction* of a new conductor.
The company has drifted for years without clear *direction*.
He felt his life lacked *direction* after graduation.

senses.gloss: Money paid regularly by the government or an insurer to someone who cannot work.
examples: He's been on *disability* since the accident.
Her *disability* check arrives on the third of the month.
She applied for *disability* after the second surgery.

senses.gloss: A complete failure, or something that has gone badly wrong.
examples: The dinner party was a *disaster* from start to finish.
His first attempt at cutting my hair was a *disaster*.
The movie was a box-office *disaster*.

senses.gloss: A flow of liquid, gas, or electricity coming out of something.
examples: The plant was fined for its *discharge* into the river.
A yellow *discharge* from the eye can mean an infection.
The lightning bolt was a single enormous electrical *discharge*.

senses.gloss: A branch of knowledge or a field of study.
examples: The conference brought together scholars from a dozen *disciplines*.
Economics is a younger *discipline* than physics.
The program lets students combine two *disciplines*.
